text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.64% today, reversing a sharp four-day slide that had cost the stock 3% since last Thursday. The bounce came as oil prices stabilized—U.S. crude held at $83.90 per barrel—after a week dominated by escalating Iran sanctions and concerns about the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint. The U.S. Navy's blockade of Iranian oil exports and Treasury action against banks facilitating Iran trade had earlier weighed on the stock, likely on worry that economic sanctions could destabilize the region or trigger retaliatory disruption of the critical shipping lane through which roughly one-third of global seaborne oil passes.

The modest recovery reflects oil prices finding a floor despite the geopolitical friction. A refiner and producer like ConocoPhillips benefits when crude prices stabilize, even if at lower levels than earlier in the month—and the news cycle shifted slightly toward diplomatic overtures (Iran saying diplomacy "isn't impossible") rather than imminent military action, which may have eased the immediate risk premium that drove the recent selloff.
